front.title: ChaCha20 and Poly1305 for IETF Protocols

abstract.t: A profile of RFC 8439 for nish/crypto/chacha20poly1305: the ChaCha20 block and stream functions, Poly1305, its key generation and the AEAD_CHACHA20_POLY1305 construction. Every requirement quotes RFC 8439, the main source; every binding sentence of RFC 8439 (MUST, MUST NOT, SHALL, SHALL NOT, REQUIRED) is tested or excluded here.

section.name: Introduction
section.t: The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "NOT RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in BCP 14 when, and only when, they appear in all capitals, as shown here.

nish/crypto/chacha20poly1305 exports each building block of RFC 8439 as well as the AEAD, so the properties can state the AEAD in terms of them. Each returns u8[] | null; the properties test null only where they say so.

section.name: Interface
section.sourcecode: // module: nish/crypto/chacha20poly1305 export const chacha20Block = (key: u8[], counter: u32, nonce: u8[]): u8[] | null export const chacha20 = (key: u8[], counter: u32, nonce: u8[], data: u8[]): u8[] | null export const poly1305 = (key: u8[], msg: u8[]): u8[] | null export const poly1305KeyGen = (key: u8[], nonce: u8[]): u8[] | null export const chacha20Poly1305Seal = (key: u8[], nonce: u8[], aad: u8[], plaintext: u8[]): u8[] | null export const chacha20Poly1305Open = (key: u8[], nonce: u8[], aad: u8[], sealed: u8[]): u8[] | null

section.name: The ChaCha20 Block Function

blockquote.t: The output is 64 random-looking bytes.
Words 13-15 are a nonce, which MUST not be repeated for the same key.

section.t: Untested: an obligation on the caller: a pure function cannot see its other invocations

blockquote.t: ChaCha20 successively calls the ChaCha20 block function, with the same key and nonce, and with successively increasing block counter parameters. ChaCha20 then serializes the resulting state by writing the numbers in little-endian order, creating a keystream block. Concatenating the keystream blocks from the successive blocks forms a keystream. The ChaCha20 function then performs an XOR of this keystream with the plaintext.

section.name: The Poly1305 Algorithm

blockquote.t: Poly1305 takes a 32-byte one-time key and a message and produces a 16-byte tag.
The pair (r,s) should be unique, and MUST be unpredictable for each invocation

section.t: Untested: the AEAD derives (r,s) per invocation from key and nonce (P-KEYGEN-IS-BLOCK0, P-TAG-IS-POLY1305); unpredictability is a property of the key, which no functional test observes

section.name: Generating the Poly1305 Key Using ChaCha20

blockquote.t: We take the first 256 bits of the serialized state, and use those as the one- time Poly1305 key
Any document that specifies the use of Poly1305 as a MAC algorithm for some protocol MUST specify that 256 bits are allocated for the integrity key.

section.t: Untested: an obligation on protocol specifications, not on this module

blockquote.t: This MUST be unique per invocation with the same key, so it MUST NOT be randomly generated.

section.t: Untested: nonce management is the caller's

blockquote.t: First, a Poly1305 one-time key is generated from the 256-bit key and nonce using the procedure described in Section 2.6.
Next, the ChaCha20 encryption function is called to encrypt the plaintext, using the same key and nonce, and with the initial counter set to 1.
padding1 -- the padding is up to 15 zero bytes, and it brings the total length so far to an integral multiple of 16.
The length of the additional data in octets (as a 64-bit little-endian integer). * The length of the ciphertext in octets (as a 64-bit little- endian integer).
A ciphertext of the same length as the plaintext. o A 128-bit tag, which is the output of the Poly1305 function.
The roles of ciphertext and plaintext are reversed, so the ChaCha20 encryption function is applied to the ciphertext, producing the plaintext.
The calculated tag is bitwise compared to the received tag. The message is authenticated if and only if the tags match.
K_LEN (key length) is 32 octets.
N_MIN = N_MAX = 12 octets.

section.name: Security Considerations

blockquote.t: any protocol using this algorithm MUST include the complete tag to minimize the opportunity for forgery.
Tag truncation MUST NOT be done.
The Poly1305 key MUST be unpredictable to an attacker.

section.t: Untested: key management is the caller's

blockquote.t: implementation MUST use a constant-time comparison function rather than relying on optimized but insecure library functions such as the C language's memcmp().

section.t: Untested: timing is not observable by a functional test; nish checks it on the emitted machine code (tests/cases/ct_asm_chacha20poly1305.ts, docs/security/crypto-aead.md)

section.sourcecode: // P-TAMPER-SEALED covers R-AUTH — flipping any one bit of the ciphertext or tag is refused forall (key: u8[] /* 32..32 */, nonce: u8[] /* 12..12 */, aad: u8[] /* 0..40 */, pt: u8[] /* 0..100 */, bit: i32 /* 0..927 */) => chacha20Poly1305Open(key, nonce, aad, flipBit(unwrap(chacha20Poly1305Seal(key, nonce, aad, pt)), bit)) === null where bit < 8 * (pt.length + 16)

// P-TAMPER-AAD covers R-AUTH — flipping any one bit of the AAD is refused forall (key: u8[] /* 32..32 */, nonce: u8[] /* 12..12 */, aad: u8[] /* 1..40 */, pt: u8[] /* 0..100 */, bit: i32 /* 0..319 */) => chacha20Poly1305Open(key, nonce, flipBit(aad, bit), unwrap(chacha20Poly1305Seal(key, nonce, aad, pt))) === null where bit < 8 * aad.length

front.title: ChaCha20 and Poly1305 for IETF Protocols

abstract.t: This document defines the ChaCha20 stream cipher as well as the use of the Poly1305 authenticator, both as stand-alone algorithms and as a "combined mode", or Authenticated Encryption with Associated Data (AEAD) algorithm.

RFC 7539, the predecessor of this document, was meant to serve as a stable reference and an implementation guide. It was a product of the Crypto Forum Research Group (CFRG). This document merges the errata filed against RFC 7539 and adds a little text to the Security Considerations section.

front.title: Key words for use in RFCs to Indicate Requirement Levels

abstract.t: In many standards track documents several words are used to signify the requirements in the specification. These words are often capitalized. This document defines these words as they should be interpreted in IETF documents. This document specifies an Internet Best Current Practices for the Internet Community, and requests discussion and suggestions for improvements.

front.title: Ambiguity of Uppercase vs Lowercase in RFC 2119 Key Words

abstract.t: RFC 2119 specifies common key words that may be used in protocol specifications. This document aims to reduce the ambiguity by clarifying that only UPPERCASE usage of the key words have the defined special meanings.
